utterance: Hi there, I'm so glad you're here. I want you to know this space is safe—whatever you're feeling or thinking, it's welcome here without judgment. I'm really curious about what's on your mind today. What brings you in for this session?

Hi there, I'm so glad you're here. I really appreciate you being open about this.  

I’ve been stuck in this loop for a while—just scrolling through things, feeling like I’m slowly rotting in bed, and it’s weird because I know I *could* do something, but I just can’t seem to start. It’s not like I don’t care or want to change—I do. But everyone around me seems to have just given up or moved on, and I feel like I’m the only one still trying to hold on. That makes it harder. I’ve been thinking about joining some kind of accountability group or starting my own, but I don’t know where to begin or if it’s even worth it. I just need someone to hear me say it out loud: I want to get better, but I don’t know how to start.  

What do you think?

It sounds like you’ve been carrying this weight of feeling stuck, even when you know you *could* change — and that the sense of being the only one trying really adds to your frustration. I can see how hard it must be to keep showing up when everyone else seems to have moved on. The fact that you're thinking about joining a group or starting one shows real courage — it means you’re not just waiting for things to get better, you’re actively trying to build something new.  

Would it be helpful to explore that idea a little more — what would that group look like, or what part of your life do you think it might help with first?

It’s hard to even imagine what that group would look like — like, who would it be with? I don’t want to just show up and feel like I’m adding to the noise or being judged. I’ve tried small groups before, and it felt like everyone was already doing it better than me, so I’d just melt into the background. And I’m scared that if I start something, I’ll fail and then feel like I’ve wasted my time. But… I also don’t want to keep doing nothing. So the real question is: how do I start without feeling like I’m already falling behind?  

Would it be okay to start small — like just a text chain with one person, maybe someone I trust, to check in every day? Just to see if that kind of connection helps, before going bigger?

Starting with just one person feels safer — like a quiet step into the light instead of a leap. I’m not sure I could handle a group right now, not with all the self-doubt and fear of failing. But if I can keep checking in with someone I trust, even just a simple message like “I’m here today” or “I didn’t do it, but I tried,” that might actually be enough to stop me from feeling completely alone.  

I wonder if that small check-in could become a kind of ritual — something I do before I go to bed, like a promise to myself. Would that feel possible?

That makes so much sense — starting small doesn’t have to be perfect, just honest. The fact that you’re naming your fear of failing, and still wanting to try, already shows how much courage you’re carrying. A simple message like “I’m here today” isn’t about doing anything right — it’s about showing up, which feels like a real win in itself.  

Would it be helpful to pick someone you feel safe with — maybe someone who knows you and isn’t expecting anything from you — and just start that check-in? Even if it’s just once a week, it could be a quiet anchor in the chaos.

I really want to try, but I’m still nervous about picking someone — like, what if they feel bad or think I’m asking for too much? I don’t want to be the person who shows up and then vanishes again, or the one who makes others feel guilty. And honestly, I don’t know if I’d even be able to keep it going without falling back into the old patterns.  

Maybe starting with someone I already know — like a friend I don’t talk to much — could work. Not to fix anything, just to say, “I’m here, and I’m trying.” If they don’t respond, or if it feels awkward, that’s okay too. I just don’t want to start something that feels like pressure.  

Would that feel okay — to try it, but not make it a big deal?

Yeah, that feels really doable — not demanding anything, just showing up in a quiet way. I think if I pick someone I already know, even if it’s just a text like “I’m here today,” it won’t feel like a burden at all. It’ll just be a small thread of honesty, and if they don’t reply, or if it feels awkward, that’s fine — I won’t expect anything.  

The thing is, I don’t need to do it perfectly. I just need to know I’m not alone in this. So if I start with that one friend — someone who wouldn’t judge me — maybe that little gesture becomes a kind of anchor.  

Would you be okay with that? I’m not pushing anything — just asking if it feels like a step worth taking.

I think that’s exactly the right kind of step — small, quiet, not demanding anything. I’ve been so used to thinking I have to “do it right” or “fix myself” that just saying “I’m here today” feels like a real break from that.  

And honestly, if I send it to someone I already know — like the friend I don’t talk to much — it won’t feel like a burden at all. It’ll just be me showing up, even if it’s just a whisper. I don’t want to make it big, or expect anything in return. If they don’t reply, or if it feels awkward, that’s okay — I’m not counting on it.  

But the fact that I’m even considering it… that already feels like progress. So yes, I think it’s worth trying. Just as a tiny thread, not a rope.

It’s strange how something so small can feel so big — like a tiny spark in a room full of dark corners. I’ve been lying in bed for days, scrolling through doom loops and thinking I’d never get out, and now the thought of just sending one message feels almost like rebellion.  

I still worry it’ll feel awkward — like I’m making someone feel bad, or that they’ll just ignore it. But maybe that’s okay too. Maybe the point isn’t for them to reply, but for me to finally stop pretending I’m not struggling.  

So if I send it — just one text — I’m not asking for anything. I’m just trying to prove to myself that I’m still here. That feels like the most honest thing I can do right now.

Yeah, it’s like the room is still dark, but now there’s a single light I didn’t know I could turn on. I don’t even know if I’ll be able to send it — my hands feel heavy, like they’re made of cotton — but the thought of just doing it, even if it’s just one word, feels like a win.

Maybe it’s not about them noticing. Maybe it’s just about me realizing — for the first time in a long time — that I don’t have to be invisible. Even if no one replies, even if I’m still stuck in bed tomorrow, that one small thing… it already changes something inside me. And that? That’s enough.

Yeah, and I think that’s the part I’ve been missing — not needing anyone to see me, or to fix me. Just knowing I showed up, even if it was quiet, even if it was just a text that might never leave the screen… that’s something.  

I still feel like I’m walking through fog, but at least now I know I’m not alone in it. And maybe, just maybe, that quiet step — that tiny act of honesty — is what starts the fog from clearing, one breath at a time.
